statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-42504 (GO-2026-5038): in the Go standard library's mime package, WordDecoder.DecodeHeader takes quadratic time on a header with many invalid encoded-words. It is fixed in Go 1.25.11 and 1.26.4: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5038, https://go.dev/issue/79217, https://go.dev/cl/774481, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/tKs3rmcBcKw . We downloaded every build-dev package that the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository lists for x86_64 and aarch64 on 2026-11-27 and checked each download against its index checksum: 92 versions, 2.6.4-r0 to the current 2.30.0-r1, each for both architectures, except 2.6.4-r0, which is published for aarch64 only. The index lists 2.19.1-r1 three times, each entry with the same source commit and installed size; the copy the repository serves was read. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/build, a statically linked Go program built for Linux (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). The programs are built with Go 1.25.7 to 1.26.11, but none of them contains the vulnerable code: in every build the function table (pclntab) of every Go program lists no mime.(*WordDecoder) method, while it lists other functions of the mime package, such as mime.ParseMediaType. WordDecoder.DecodeHeader is not linked into any program, so the vulnerable code is not present.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42504 (GO-2026-5038): in the Go standard library's mime package, WordDecoder.DecodeHeader moved past only the leading =? of an encoded-word it could not decode and then searched the rest of the header again, so a header with many invalid encoded-words takes quadratic time to decode, a denial of service. The fix skips the whole undecodable encoded-word. It is fixed in Go 1.25.11 and 1.26.4: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5038, https://go.dev/issue/79217, https://go.dev/cl/774481, the release-branch.go1.26 backport https://github.com/golang/go/commit/7f24db453a60faf6a3546d60bb02917a0a7aace0 (in go1.26.4, not go1.26.3), https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/tKs3rmcBcKw . The master commit https://github.com/golang/go/commit/f230dd8a1d0a63d73e92685e378dcd725f7aac00 is in go1.27.0, so every Go 1.27 release carries the fix. We downloaded every external-dns-dev package listed in the Alpine 3.23 index of the DHI Alpine repository, for x86_64 and aarch64: 33 versions from 0.20.0-r0 to the current 0.24.0-r5, each published for both architectures, and checked each download against the index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/external-dns, a Go program built with GOOS=linux and CGO_ENABLED=0, plus directories; no package contains a symbolic link. We read the function table (pclntab) and build information of the program in every build and searched its bytes, which also finds the names of inlined functions; runtime.main is in the function table of every build. The Go release by build: 0.20.0-r0 Go 1.25.7; 0.20.0-r1 to 0.21.0-r0 Go 1.26.1; 0.21.0-r1 to 0.21.0-r2 Go 1.26.2; 0.21.0-r3 to 0.21.0-r5 Go 1.26.3; 0.21.0-r6 to 0.21.0-r7 Go 1.26.4; 0.21.0-r8 to 0.21.0-r11 Go 1.26.5; 0.21.0-r12 Go 1.26.6; 0.21.0-r13 to 0.22.0-r0 Go 1.26.7; 0.22.0-r1 to 0.22.0-r3 Go 1.26.8; 0.23.0-r1 to 0.23.0-r2 Go 1.27.1; 0.23.0-r3 Go 1.27.2; 0.23.0-r4 to 0.24.0-r2 Go 1.27.3; 0.24.0-r3 to 0.24.0-r5 Go 1.27.4. The Go vulnerability database lists mime WordDecoder.DecodeHeader, and mime.(*WordDecoder).DecodeHeader is in the function table of every build. The status follows the Go release. The builds before 0.21.0-r6 (0.20.0-r0 to 0.21.0-r5) use Go 1.25.7, 1.26.1, 1.26.2 or 1.26.3, inside the affected range; 0.21.0-r6 and every later build use Go 1.26.4 to 1.26.8 or 1.27.1 to 1.27.4, which carry the fix, so 0.21.0-r6 is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-42504 (GO-2026-5038): in the Go standard library's mime package, WordDecoder.DecodeHeader moved past only the leading =? of an encoded-word it could not decode and then searched the rest of the header again, so a header with many invalid encoded-words takes quadratic time to decode, a denial of service. The fix skips the whole undecodable encoded-word. It is fixed in Go 1.25.11 and 1.26.4: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5038, https://go.dev/issue/79217, https://go.dev/cl/774481, the release-branch.go1.26 backport https://github.com/golang/go/commit/7f24db453a60faf6a3546d60bb02917a0a7aace0 (in go1.26.4, not go1.26.3), https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/tKs3rmcBcKw . The master commit https://github.com/golang/go/commit/f230dd8a1d0a63d73e92685e378dcd725f7aac00 is in go1.27.0, so every Go 1.27 release carries the fix. We downloaded every external-dns package listed in the Alpine 3.23 index of the DHI Alpine repository, for x86_64 and aarch64: 33 versions from 0.20.0-r0 to the current 0.24.0-r5, each published for both architectures, and checked each download against the index checksum. It is fixed in Go 1.25.11 and 1.26.4: https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-5038, https://go.dev/issue/79217, https://go.dev/cl/774481, https://groups.google.com/g/golang-announce/c/tKs3rmcBcKw . We read the file list and MD5 checksums (the md5sums control file) of every build-dev package listed in the Debian 13 index of the DHI Debian repository on 2026-11-27, for amd64 and arm64: 67 versions, 2.13.0-1 to the current 2.30.0-1. Every file in each of them has the same MD5 checksum as the file at the same path in the DHI Alpine 3.23 package of the same version and architecture (2.26.0-1 and 2.26.0-r1, for example), so the programs below were read from those Alpine packages. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/build, a statically linked Go program built for Linux (no program interpreter and no shared-library dependencies). The programs are built with Go 1.26.2 to 1.26.11, but none of them contains the vulnerable code: in every build the function table (pclntab) of every Go program lists no mime.(*WordDecoder) method, while it lists other functions of the mime package, such as mime.ParseMediaType. WordDecoder.DecodeHeader is not linked into any program, so the vulnerable code is not present.
